segregation.statement: Two affected family members carry the variant (P16 and P17, family 7). The paper notes P16 was refractory while other carrier members had mild symptoms. Unaffected relatives tested: not reported; the pedigree text shows a symbol (‡) for a non-analyzed asymptomatic carrier in family 7, but the layout is garbled.

quotes.quote: | F7 | P16 | M | 0 mo | p.A588VfsX | Mesalazine, CS, IFX, ETN, GLM, enterectomy, endoscopic balloon dilation | Colchicine, PSL, thalidomide, MTX, ADA | (7,13) |
Regarding severity, in three families (families 1, 3 and 7), patients 1, 4 and 16 presented with refractory disease, whereas other members with pathogenic variants exhibited only mild symptoms.
<sup>‡</sup>Non-analyzed genetically predisposed asymptomatic carrier of heterozygous *TNFAIP3* variants.

functional.statement: No assay result for this specific variant is stated in the text of 40574834. The paper says newly identified variants were tested with an NF-kB reporter assay in A20-deficient HEK293 cells (construct) and shown in Figure 2, and that diagnosis required functional confirmation, but the figure's variant labels are not in the text available here. These quotes are cohort-level.

quotes.quote: The results of functional analyses of newly identified TNFAIP3 variants are shown in Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 2.
The diagnosis of HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift deletion of 11 nucleotides, predicted p.(Ala588ValfsTer80) per the batch HGVS. The paper attributes the disease to heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).
All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Numbering: the paper writes c.1760_1770del11; the batch HGVS is c.1763_1773del (3 nt further 3′). The protein (p.Ala588ValfsX80) agrees with the batch prediction, which fits a 3′ shift within a repeat, but the paper does not say so; the panel should confirm the two strings describe the same deletion.
P16 and P17 relationship (e.g. parent and child) is not stated in the text; the pedigree figure text is garbled.
P16 is also cited to reference 13 (Mitsunaga et al. 2023), a primary report not in this batch.
Survey tables only; no case narrative.
notes_for_panel: Two affected carriers in one family. A ‡ symbol in the family 7 pedigree text suggests an untested asymptomatic obligate carrier, which the panel should check in the figure.
